name: Cobalt Group
summary: Cobalt Group is a financially motivated threat group that has primarily targeted financial institutions since at least 2016. The group has conducted intrusions to steal money via targeting ATM systems, card processing, payment systems and SWIFT systems. Cobalt Group has mainly targeted banks in Eastern Europe, Central Asia, and Southeast Asia. One of the alleged leaders was arrested in Spain in early 2018, but the group still appears to be active. The group has been known to target organizations in order to use their access to then compromise additional victims. Reporting indicates there may be links between Cobalt Group and both the malware Carbanak and the group Carbanak.

procedures.text: Cobalt Group has obtained and used a variety of tools including Mimikatz, PsExec, Cobalt Strike, and SDelete.
Cobalt Group has sent emails with URLs pointing to malicious documents.
Cobalt Group has compromised legitimate web browser updates to deliver a backdoor.

Cobalt Group has sent spearphishing emails with various attachment types to corporate and personal email accounts of victim organizations. Attachment types have included.rtf,.doc,.xls, archives containing LNK files, and password protected archives containing.exe and.scr executables.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use known credentials to run commands and spawn processes as a domain user account.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use known credentials to run commands and spawn processes as a local user account.
Cobalt Group has used a JavaScript backdoor that is capable of launching cmd.exe to execute shell commands. The group has used an exploit toolkit known as Threadkit that launches.bat files.
Cobalt Group has executed JavaScript scriptlets on the victim's machine.
Cobalt Group has used powershell.exe to download and execute scripts.
Cobalt Group has sent Word OLE compound documents with malicious obfuscated VBA macros that will run upon user execution.

Cobalt Group had exploited multiple vulnerabilities for execution, including Microsoft’s Equation Editor (CVE-2017-11882), an Internet Explorer vulnerability (CVE-2018-8174), CVE-2017-8570, CVE-2017-0199, and CVE-2017-8759.
Cobalt Group has sent emails containing malicious links that require users to execute a file or macro to infect the victim machine.
Cobalt Group has created Windows tasks to establish persistence.
Cobalt Group has sent emails containing malicious attachments that require users to execute a file or macro to infect the victim machine.
Cobalt Group has sent malicious Word OLE compound documents to victims.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use PsExec to execute a payload on a remote host. It can also use Service Control Manager to start new services.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use WMI to deliver a payload to a remote host.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use Python to perform execution.

Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike's Beacon payload is capable of running shell commands without `cmd.exe` and PowerShell commands without `powershell.exe` Cobalt Strike can also use `CreateThreadpoolWait`, `SetThreadpoolWait`, and `MessageBoxA` for sandbox evasion and execution of embedded payloads in memory.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can download a hosted "beacon" payload using BITSAdmin.
Cobalt Group has created new services to establish persistence.
Cobalt Group has added persistence by registering the file name for the next stage malware under `HKCU\Environment\UserInitMprLogonScript`.
Cobalt Group has used Registry Run keys for persistence. The group has also set a Startup path to launch the PowerShell shell command and download Cobalt Strike.

Mimikatz: The Mimikatz credential dumper has been extended to include Skeleton Key domain controller authentication bypass functionality. The `LSADUMP::ChangeNTLM` and `LSADUMP::SetNTLM` modules can also manipulate the password hash of an account without knowing the clear text value.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can modify Registry values within `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Office\<Excel Version>\Excel\Security\AccessVBOM\` to enable the execution of additional code.
PsExec: PsExec has the ability to remotely create accounts on target systems.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike has the ability to use an Excel Workbook to execute additional code by enabling Office to trust macros and execute code without user permission.
Mimikatz: The Mimikatz credential dumper contains an implementation of an SSP.
Cobalt Group has injected code into trusted processes.
Cobalt Group has used exploits to increase their levels of rights and privileges.
Cobalt Group has bypassed UAC.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike has the ability to load DLLs via reflective injection.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use process hollowing for execution.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can steal access tokens from exiting processes.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can make tokens from known credentials.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can spawn processes with alternate PPIDs.

Mimikatz: Mimikatz's `MISC::AddSid` module can append any SID or user/group account to a user's SID-History. Mimikatz also utilizes SID-History Injection to expand the scope of other components such as generated Kerberos Golden Tickets and DCSync beyond a single domain.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use `sudo` to run a command.
Cobalt Group deleted the DLL dropper from the victim’s machine to cover their tracks.
Cobalt Group has used regsvr32.exe to execute scripts.
Cobalt Group obfuscated several scriptlets and code used on the victim’s machine, including through use of XOR and RC4.
More_eggs: More_eggs will decode malware components that are then dropped to the system.
Cobalt Group has used the command `cmstp.exe /s /ns C:\Users\ADMINI~W\AppData\Local\Temp\XKNqbpzl.txt` to bypass AppLocker and launch a malicious script.
Cobalt Group has used `odbcconf` to proxy the execution of malicious DLL files.
Cobalt Group used msxsl.exe to bypass AppLocker and to invoke Jscript code from an XSL file.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can hash functions to obfuscate calls to the Windows API and use a public/private key pair to encrypt Beacon session metadata.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike includes a capability to modify the Beacon payload to eliminate known signatures or unpacking methods.
More_eggs: More_eggs's payload has been encrypted with a key that has the hostname and processor family information appended to the end.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can timestomp any files or payloads placed on a target machine to help them blend in.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use `rundll32.exe` to load DLL from the command line.
Cobalt Strike: The Cobalt Strike loader can use the `MessageBoxA` API to prompt for user interaction as an anti-sandbox measure.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use spoof arguments in spawned processes that execute beacon commands.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike's `execute-assembly` command can run a.NET executable within the memory of a sacrificial process by loading the CLR.
More_eggs: More_eggs has used a signed binary shellcode loader and a signed Dynamic Link Library (DLL) to create a reverse shell.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz’s `LSADUMP::DCShadow` module can be used to make AD updates by temporarily setting a computer to be a DC.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike has the ability to use Smart Applet attacks to disable the Java SecurityManager sandbox.

Mimikatz: Mimikatz performs credential dumping to obtain account and password information useful in gaining access to additional systems and enterprise network resources. It contains functionality to acquire information about credentials in many ways, including from the LSASS Memory.

procedures.text: Mimikatz: Mimikatz contains functionality to acquire credentials from the Windows Credential Manager.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's kerberos module can create golden tickets.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's kerberos module can create silver tickets.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's `CRYPTO` module can create and export various types of authentication certificates.
Cobalt Group used a JavaScript backdoor that is capable of collecting a list of the security solutions installed on the victim's machine.
More_eggs: More_eggs has the capability to gather the IP address from the victim's machine.
Cobalt Group leveraged an open-source tool called SoftPerfect Network Scanner to perform network scanning.
SpicyOmelette: SpicyOmelette can identify payment systems, payment gateways, and ATM systems in compromised environments.
More_eggs: More_eggs has the capability to gather the OS version and computer name.
SpicyOmelette: SpicyOmelette can enumerate running software on a targeted system.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can enumerate services on compromised hosts.

Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can query `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Office\<Excel Version>\Excel\Security\AccessVBOM\` to determine if the security setting for restricting default programmatic access is enabled.
More_eggs: More_eggs has used HTTP GET requests to check internet connectivity.
More_eggs: More_eggs has the capability to gather the username from the victim's machine.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can produce a sessions report from compromised hosts.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike's Beacon payload can collect information on process details.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use `net localgroup` to list local groups on a system.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can identify targets by querying account groups on a domain contoller.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can explore files on a compromised system.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can determine if the user on an infected machine is in the admin or domain admin group.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can query shared drives on the local system.
Cobalt Group has used Remote Desktop Protocol to conduct lateral movement.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use Window admin shares (C$ and ADMIN$) for lateral movement.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's `SEKURLSA::Pth` module can impersonate a user, with only a password hash, to execute arbitrary commands.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can deliver Beacon payloads for lateral movement by leveraging remote COM execution.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can SSH to a remote service.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use `WinRM` to execute a payload on a remote host.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz’s `LSADUMP::DCSync` and `KERBEROS::PTT` modules implement the three steps required to extract the krbtgt account hash and create/use Kerberos tickets.
PsExec: PsExec can be used to download or upload a file over a network share.
SpicyOmelette: SpicyOmelette has collected data and other information from a compromised host.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike's Beacon payload is capable of capturing screenshots.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can perform browser pivoting and inject into a user's browser to inherit cookies, authenticated HTTP sessions, and client SSL certificates.

Cobalt Group has used public sites such as github.com and sendspace.com to upload files and then download them to victim computers. The group's JavaScript backdoor is also capable of downloading files.
Cobalt Group has used HTTPS for C2.
Cobalt Group has used DNS tunneling for C2.
Cobalt Group has used the Plink utility to create SSH tunnels.
Cobalt Group has used the Plink utility to create SSH tunnels.
More_eggs: More_eggs has used basE91 encoding, along with encryption, for C2 communication.
Cobalt Group used the Ammyy Admin tool as well as TeamViewer for remote access, including to preserve remote access if a Cobalt Strike module was lost.
More_eggs: More_eggs has used an RC4-based encryption method for its C2 communications.

Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can leverage the HTTP protocol for C2 communication, while hiding the actual data in either an HTTP header, URI parameter, the transaction body, or appending it to the URI. Cobalt Strike
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can conduct peer-to-peer communication over Windows named pipes encapsulated in the SMB protocol. All protocols use their standard assigned ports.

Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can be configured to have commands relayed over a peer-to-peer network of infected hosts. This can be used to limit the number of egress points, or provide access to a host without direct internet access.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike has the ability to accept a value for HTTP Host Header to enable domain fronting.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can be configured to use TCP, ICMP, and UDP for C2 communications.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can set its Beacon payload to reach out to the C2 server on an arbitrary and random interval.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike will break large data sets into smaller chunks for exfiltration.
SDelete: SDelete deletes data in a way that makes it unrecoverable.
